findings.title: canManage() falls back to the VIEW scope, so a view-only admin can manage groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) returns true when `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` succeeds. Since the check passes if EITHER scope is granted, an admin who was only granted the `view` scope on the Groups resource (or on the all-groups type resource) will have canManage() return true. This evaluator backs GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()/requireManage(), GroupResource.deleteGroup() and other manage checks, so a view-only admin can create, modify and delete groups. The fallback should only accept the MANAGE scope (as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does on line 79).

findings.title: hasPermission can NPE when the 'Groups' type resource is missing
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when no per-group resource is found, `resource` is reassigned from AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null when the resource-server is not the admin-permissions client, when admin permissions are disabled, or simply when the 'Groups' type resource has not been created / was deleted. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which depending on the store implementation throws a NullPointerException and turns every group permission check into a 500 error. A null check (returning false) is missing after the fallback lookup.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission no longer honors manage permission, hiding manageable users from search
findings.body: The early-return in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (and the equivalent change in GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) only checks `root.users().canView()`. Previously (V1 getGroupsWithViewPermission) the check was `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()`. In V2, an admin can hold the all-users `manage` permission without `view`: UserPermissionsV2.canManage(UserModel) accepts MANAGE, and canView(user) accepts VIEW or MANAGE, so per-user checks say the admin can see/manage every user. But getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns the (empty) set of group permissions, so UsersResource.searchForUser sets UserModel.GROUPS to an empty set and getUsersCount(..., groupIds) counts 0 — the admin's user search and count return nothing even though the admin can manage all users. The early-return should also treat users().canManage() as unrestricted, or the per-user/per-type view evaluation should be used.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission evaluates a full policy evaluation per group resource
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission iterates all resources of type 'Groups' via resourceStore.findByType and, for each one, runs a complete authorization policy evaluation through hasPermission (which itself does another resourceStore lookup and evaluatePermission). In realms with many groups and many per-group permissions this makes every user search/count call (UsersResource.getUsers/searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) perform N full policy evaluations, which can be very expensive. The old V1 implementation had the same shape, but now that per-group resources are expected to be created routinely for FGAP v2 this should be batched or cached per request.
